message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium) |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV (first) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV (negative, so H⁻ is unstable in vacuum) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Atomic radius | ~31 pm (covalent) |
| | Van der Waals radius | ~120 pm |
| **Physical State (298 K, 1 atm)** | State | Gas |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (−423.17 °F) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (−434.69 °F) |
| | Density | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Specific heat (Cp) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Heat of vaporization | 0.449 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Speed of sound | ~1270 m s⁻¹ (in H₂) |
| | Refractive index | 1.000132 (at 589 nm) |
| | Viscosity | 8.76 × 10⁻⁶ Pa s |
| | Thermal conductivity | 0.180 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| **Chemical Properties** | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride), 0 (H₂) |
| | Bonding | Forms covalent bonds; H₂ is a diatomic molecule with a single σ bond |
| | Reactivity | Highly reactive; forms hydrides with metals, acids with nonmetals, and oxidizes to water or oxides |
| | Acid–base behavior | Acts as a weak acid (H⁺ donor) in aqueous solution; forms hydronium (H₃O⁺) |
| | Redox behavior | Reducing agent (e.g., H₂ + O₂ → H₂O); oxidized to H⁺ in acids |
| | Combustion | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic, ΔH ≈ –286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Spectroscopy | Strong absorption in UV (Lyman series), visible (Balmer series), IR (vibrational transitions) |
| | Isotopic effects | Deuterium and tritium shift vibrational frequencies; used in isotope labeling and nuclear fusion |
| **Physical Chemistry** | Dissociation energy (H₂) | 4.478 eV (432 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Bond length (H₂) | 0.741 Å |
| | Dipole moment | 0 D (homonuclear diatomic) |
| | Polarizability | 0.666 Å³ |
| | Rotational constant (H₂) | 60.853 cm⁻¹ |
| | Vibrational frequency (H₂) | 4401 cm⁻¹ |
| **Astrophysical & Industrial Relevance** | Stellar fusion | Proton–proton chain (p + p → d + e⁺ + νₑ) |
| | Fusion fuel | Deuterium–tritium (DT) reaction: D + T → He‑4 + n + 17.6 MeV |
| | Energy storage | Hydrogen fuel cells (electrochemical conversion of H₂ to electricity) |
| | Space propulsion | Liquid hydrogen (LH₂) used as rocket propellant (e.g., Saturn V, Space Shuttle) |
| | Environmental impact | Zero CO₂ emissions when combusted; requires renewable electricity for green H₂ production |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: atomic number 1, mass ~1 u, extremely low density.
- **Highly reactive**: forms hydrides, acids, and fuels; oxidizes readily.
- **Diatomic gas**: H₂ is the most stable form under normal conditions.
- **Key isotope roles**: Deuterium (heavy hydrogen) used in nuclear fusion and as a tracer; Tritium (radioactive) used in fusion research and as a tracer in biology.
- **Energy carrier**: Hydrogen fuel cells produce electricity with only water as a by‑product; LH₂ is a powerful rocket propellant.
- **Spectroscopic marker**: Hydrogen lines (Lyman, Balmer) are fundamental in astronomy for identifying stellar compositions.

Feel free to ask for deeper details on any specific property or application!
